title: Value Validation and Computation knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Value Validation and Computation”?
options: Specified, computed, used, and actual values
questions.answer_key: Specified, computed, used, and actual values
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “Specified, computed, used, and actual values” under “Value Validation and Computation”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with value validation and computation?
options: Use the smallest valid example, prefer a readable default, and check browser behavior rather than trusting appearance alone.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Use the smallest valid example, prefer a readable default, and check browser behavior rather than trusting appearance alone.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Use the smallest valid example, prefer a readable default, and check browser behavior rather than trusting appearance alone. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “Value Validation and Computation” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
